units.text: INT. DROWNED CATHEDRAL - NAVE - TWILIGHT
Seawater fills the cathedral to the height of a man's knee, black and perfectly still.
Through the shattered rose window a violet sky bleeds in.
Pews rise from the flood like the ribs of some enormous animal, and pale lantern-fish drift between them, trailing threads of cold light.
A flat-bottomed boat noses between the pillars.
In the stern, a woman poles steadily, her coat the green of old copper.
In the bow sits a man with a ledger across his knees, and between them, a girl hugs a birdcage covered in cloth.
Mind the altar rail. It bites.
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: It does not bite. It is a rail.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: It took my last pole in half.
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: Because you steered it into the rail.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: The girl has not spoken.
She watches the water as though something might rise out of it.
Under the cloth, something in the cage shifts and murmurs.
It's awake.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: It's not awake.
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: It is certainly awake.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: It wants out.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: They always want out, love. That's the nature of--
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: We agreed that it stays covered until the choir loft.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: We agreed nothing. You agreed. I poled.
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: He closes the ledger with a snap.
She leans harder into the pole.
The boat glides through a drift of drowned hymn-books, their pages spread like pale hands.
At the far end of the nave, the water begins to move.
A slow ring spreads from the base of the pulpit, then another.
The lantern-fish scatter.
Odalys sees it first.
Her grip tightens on the cage.
She says nothing.
Nerissa.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: I see it.
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: You are not looking at it.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: I am looking at everything. That is the point of looking.
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: It's under us.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: The pole stops mid-stroke.
Water drips off the end and sets small circles ringing outward.
Under the boat, something enormous and unhurried turns over in the dark.
Give it the bird.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: No.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Odalys--
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: It's mine. It sings for me.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Child, I am asking you--
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Don't ask her, Barnaby, you'll only make it worse--
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: I am being perfectly reasonable!
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: You are shouting in a church!
units.name: NERISSA

units.text: The boat lifts.
Not much.
Enough that the water slides off the hull in a sheet.
Odalys pulls the cloth from the cage in a single sweep.
Inside, a small gray wren opens its beak and sings a single, impossible note.
Every pane left in the rose window answers it.
The water goes still.
Barnaby lowers the ledger.
Nerissa lowers the pole.
Odalys, eyes shut, holds the cage up toward the light.
Slowly, the boat settles.
